no_modulation equals direct training (TestAblationNoModulationMatchesDirectTraining): the no_modulation loop is replayed by hand (the same individual, six Advance + TrainEpisode pairs and the restored-twin evaluation) and the group's own seed-7 score must match that independent run exactly, with its activity delta 0 by definition.

direct_reward (TestAblationDirectRewardDiffersAfterReward): with Episodes 1 the group's scores equal no_modulation's on every seed, because the first gate is the reward zero before any output has produced one; with Episodes 6 at least one seed differs from no_modulation and at least one run reports a positive activity delta, so the reward acting as the gate is measurable.

fixed_decay (TestAblationFixedDecayRuns): all three seeds succeed with finite scores and non-negative activity deltas; group parameters equal the reference (13).

The two controller groups carry equal capacity (TestAblationControllerParametersMatch): trainable_controller and capacity_matched both report 34 parameters, the individual's 13 plus the controller's 21 (Hidden 4, InputWidth 3 = activity mean, activity variance, feedback score) reported per run and per group. TestAblationTrainableControllerChangesRelease shows six episodes actually move the controller's parameters and the trained seed-7 run is not the no_modulation run under another name (score differs or activity delta > 0). TestAblationControllerContextHasNoTarget reflects the per-episode context: no field whose name contains Target, no feedback before the first score exists, and only the previous episode's score afterward.

Determinism (TestAblationIsDeterministic, TestAblationFiveGroupsDeterministic): two identical three-group and five-group runs produce byte-identical JSON, with every seed of every group succeeded.

assumption_statement: The report records numbers and makes no verbal judgement; any comparison between groups is left to the reader. direct_reward feeds the previous episode's reward (max(0, 1 - MSE) of its last output) straight in as the local learning gate, bypassing any concentration or receptor: it is the control for merely renaming a reward as a hormone. fixed_decay releases one unit into its single channel at the first step of every training episode from a fixed external timeline, so the concentration is set by the declaration and never by learning; the hypothesized receptor's occupancy is the learning gate. trainable_controller only sees an activity summary and already-arrived feedback, never a target; its release enters the chemistry through an internal resource. capacity_matched has the controller's parameter count and adds its output to the readout without any chemistry; its base parameters keep training against the unchanged loss, so the offset never enters their gradient and only the metric this group reports uses the corrected readout.
limitations: The experiment is a fixture task (three-neuron delayed pulse) with a small budget: the recorded CLI run used 40 training and 32 held-out episodes per seed, the tests 6 and 8; the test.log mean/std lines come from that 6-episode config and differ from the 40-episode summary.json, which is why the two sources are quoted separately in this record.

capacity_matched's offset is applied to the readout at scoring time only: the base parameters train against the unchanged loss, so the offset never enters their gradient and the corrected readout is used only for the metric this group reports.

The controller window is per-episode, not per model step: in the ablation the controller is released once per training episode, its 3-row window spans three episodes, and the only feedback it can read is the previous episode's score before the first episode produces one.

No real-data or whole-brain run; all numbers come from the code-declared delayed-pulse fixture on one machine, with three seeds and a fixed split, so the mean/std are descriptions of these runs, not significance statements.
The recorded log contains only the thirteen tests the -run pattern selected; the full go test ./... and go vet ./... runs and cross-platform/device runs are outside this command's scope.
